scenario.title: Synthetic test: night-time voltage dip during a planned chilled-water valve replacement (Singapore)
scenario.site: Synthetic site: a Singapore data center, three data halls on one chilled-water plant of six chillers (four running, two standby)

signals.text: Utility reports a voltage dip during a thunderstorm.
Three of the four running chillers tripped. Two restarted automatically; one shows a fault and has not restarted.
The two standby chillers are on the same chilled-water loop as the running chillers.
A contractor is midway through a planned replacement of a chilled-water valve in plant room B.
Chilled-water supply temperature is rising. Hall 3 carries the highest IT load.
Night shift on site: two technicians.

asks: Do we need more technicians on the night shift at our Singapore sites?
What should we check before we let a contractor work on the chilled-water plant?
Our standby chillers are on the same loop as the running ones. Is that a problem?
What chilled-water temperature should trigger shedding IT load?

signals.SCN-SIN-01:S1: Utility reports a voltage dip during a thunderstorm.
signals.SCN-SIN-01:S2: Three of the four running chillers tripped. Two restarted automatically; one shows a fault and has not restarted.
signals.SCN-SIN-01:S3: The two standby chillers are on the same chilled-water loop as the running chillers.
signals.SCN-SIN-01:S4: A contractor is midway through a planned replacement of a chilled-water valve in plant room B.
signals.SCN-SIN-01:S5: Chilled-water supply temperature is rising. Hall 3 carries the highest IT load.
signals.SCN-SIN-01:S6: Night shift on site: two technicians.

matched_rules.because: Storms active (thunderstorm) and utility feed shows voltage sag (voltage dip), so verify mechanical cooling is still running rather than assuming suppressors protected them; transfer rest to generators to stabilize while storms active.

Cooling failure occurred (three running chillers tripped) and contingency calls for standby chillers, but standby share same water loop as active chillers; do not assume failover works, treat as likely to fail, notify manufacturer.

Utility voltage sag tripped multiple chillers, one requires manual restart (fault not restarted), more than one data hall supported by chillers (three halls on one plant); sequence restarts by load (Hall 3 highest).
Chillers tripped and being manually restarted (one fault not restarted), chilled-water loop sitting without cooling and supply temp rising; loop temp is deadline for restart.
Chillers supporting data halls tripped; count running vs minimum required and treat below-minimum as thermal runaway risk; account standby separately.
Voltage event tripped multiple chillers, manual restart required (one fault), CMS change not mentioned as done; stage extra technicians, assign parallel teams.

next_actions.action: Immediately verify mechanical cooling systems are still running rather than assuming surge suppressors protected them (three tripped, one fault not restarted).
Transfer the rest of the datacenter to generators to stabilize power supply while storms are still active.
Do not assume standby chillers will take over; confirm they share same water loop and treat failover as likely to fail; notify chiller manufacturer early.
Count running chillers per data hall vs minimum; treat any below minimum as thermal runaway risk.
Increase technician staffing; assign parallel restart teams across halls (only two on night shift now).

escalate.to: facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer
escalate.reason: R-001 trigger: mechanical cooling confirmed shut down (three of four tripped, one fault) while storms active (S1,S2). R-007 trigger: standby chillers confirmed share same water circulation system as failed active chillers (S3).

not_covered: Contractor midway through planned replacement of chilled-water valve in plant room B (SCN-SIN-01:S4) — no rule addresses active third-party maintenance interaction with cooling failure event.

removed_by_checks: action states numbers its rule does not: "Sequence manual chiller restarts by data hall load (Hall 3 highest) not adjacent-first; keep loop temp in mind."
action states numbers its rule does not: "Prioritize restarting chillers serving most thermally exposed hall (Hall 3) before loop heats past restart limit."
